It has worked fine with diesel fuel over the 7 months it has been in use. One must modify the vent fitting to accommodate a diesel return line, but that is easy enough.

The tank is translucent which makes it easy, in my situation, to see the fuel level. I am not using the fuel level sensor, so cannot comment on it.

If you are considering this tank, be aware that while it claims to be 14 gallons, the actual usable capacity is about 10.4 gallons.

The cost of the tank seems high, but it is well made and more affordable than any alternatives I could find. I have owned boats and would select a Moeller fuel tank for use in a boat which needed a tank.

Tent Stakes with Storage Pouch【Upgraded】, 7’’Hexagon Rod Stakes Tent Pegs with Hook Nail Spike Garden Stakes Camping Pegs for Pitching Camping Tent Out of the box, these look like exactly what I need. I will be camping soon and will update this review if needed.

I got these to replace the large oversized nail style stakes that I've been using for years. The big nails work, but they are sometimes difficult to insert and remove and are overkill for my needs.

For general use, I think these aluminum stakes are the perfect balance between the thin pin-like stakes that come with tents and the large nail stakes. The pack of 20 gives me enough for my 6 person tent and several spares.

I like the hexagonal shape of the stakes. I expect the size and hex shape will help prevent the stake from spinning around (a problem with the thin pin-like stakes). The shape of the hook itself should also prevent spinning.

I look forward to putting these in the dirt!

Update: After a weekend camping I think these are great for soft earth like in a campground or yard. In rocky ground I expect these will bend. For sandy ground I think I would want longer stakes.

But for normal earth these are great. They are better than the thin wire stakes that come with the tent, and yet small enough to store in the tent bag. I'm glad to have these.

text_fidelity_a: MICLON Cybertrack 100 Electric Bike for Adults, 2X Faster Charge, 350W BAFANG Motor, 36V 10.4AH Removable Battery, 20MPH 26'' Mountain Ebike, Shimano 21 Speed, Suspension Fork, LED Display I'm a 75 year old man who has been riding a regular bike for years and years but my knees were telling me that hills were no longer their friend. I moved from a place with NO hills to a place where hills are everywhere so I decided to look in to an ebike that was within my budget. This bike seemed to be just what I needed so I decided to give it a shot...First thing was it was very easy to assemble (Youtube helped)..then I decided to take it for a spin. This bike is a completely different experience so my advise would be to practice in a place that's deserted...so here's the low down on my first week of riding on a regular basis....first, this bike will get up and go and reach 20 mph very fast, and for me that was my first surprise, then getting a feel for the 5 levels of resistance 1 being the most and 5 is where you hardly pedal at all, but here's where you need to pay attention....the throttle takes up about half the right handle bar so it's very easy to accelerate when you don't want to so pay attention...then there the issue with the kick stand which seems be very wobblily and a little unstable....having said that, I really like this bike, it's very easy and fun when you get used to it...quick note, I would not leave my house with charger plugged it just to be safe...So now on July 13th or having the bike for over a month the only thing that is driving me nuts is the kick stand...it flops down over and over again even after tightening the so called locking mechanism..it is aggravating and turns my bike ride into a hassle.....it's a terrible TERRIBLE design....................*******.........So I've  owned the bike almost 4 months and I continue to love this bike, I replaced the kick stand and replaced the seat with one a lot more comfortable, The one thing that, for me, makes the ride safer and more predictable is....if I'm riding near people or on roads with intersections I keep the resistance on 1 or 0 and use the hand throttle to provide power to the bike. I used to keep it on 2-4 but found that when I wanted to stop if any pressure was put on the pedals when trying to stop immediately throws the bike forward when you're not expecting it..I learned the hard way and it wasn't pretty..In my opinion controlling the bike with the hand throttle is the safest except if your riding on a trail or on a road with no stop and go...This in my opinion is the best and safest way to operate the bike with the electric assist....aside from that this is a great entry level bike at a very good price.  I look forward to many more miles of fun...
text_fidelity_b: MICLON Cybertrack 100 Electric Bike for Adults, 2X Faster Charge, 350W BAFANG Motor, 36V 10.4AH Removable Battery, 20MPH 26'' Mountain Ebike, Shimano 21 Speed, Suspension Fork, LED Display

text_fidelity_a: Ello Syndicate Glass Water Bottle with One-Touch Flip Lid I purchased this replacement item on Amazon after buying this original item in a Wegmans grocery store and then accidentally leaving it behind in public.  This water bottle has 1 specific function to me which is sooo important - and hard to find in other water bottles! - the fact that you can close and open it with only 1 hand.  I know, I know, this may sound silly, but this is EXACTLY what I wanted since I like to drink when in the car driving.  With this water bottle, I can always keep 1 hand on the steering wheel while at a stop, while grabbing the bottle for a quick sip with my other hand.  I love that feature.  A lot of bottles require the tops to be unscrewed (therefore 2 hands needed) or some kind of straw (such a pain to clean)... but not this one!  Also, the strap on this bottle is really nice as well, I like that functionality as well.  Both my husband and I have these bottles (I have the lavender and he has gray), and like I mentioned I'm on my 2nd one.  I would never buy another glass water bottle again other than this brand / model.
text_fidelity_b: Ello Syndicate Glass Water Bottle with One-Touch Flip Lid

text_fidelity_a:
JOOLA Spinforce Professional Table Tennis Racket - Competition Grade Ping Pong Paddle with Flared Handle - ITTF Tournament Approved Preassembled Table Tennis Rubber and Blade [[VIDEOID:2c69b3bfc7c1c232d95de5057a58b9ef]] This racket is great! It's the most professional racket I've ever used, and it really helps to improve your game, especially if you're used to lower quality rackets.

The surface is a little sticky. Well, not really sticky, but the contact surface with the ball is very good, which gives this a ton of accuracy. There will be no more ball slipping at crucial moments if you use this.

I really like how it's layered. The marketing materials say that there are five layers, but there are really just three layers, but repeated on both sides. So, that's why there are five total layers. I love how you can see and feel all of the layers by looking at the profile of the racket. Oh, actually, I just looked up JOOLA's website, and I must have accidentally ripped off the part that disguises the layers. The three layers are 1) the semi-sticky spongy outside, 2) a foam inner layer, and 3) a wooden center. When you squish it, is squishes just the right amount.

It's extremely lightweight. I don't know what wood they made it out of, but it's obviously a super lightweight wood.

The handle feels great. It's entirely made out of wood, with an indented Spinforce logo on one side. I like that it's indented, because I'm able to feel which side is which by touch alone.

Pros:
+Very lightweight
+Many professionally made layers
+Handle is extremely comfortable
+Looks great

Cons:
-Wooden handle might give you a few splinters until it gets worn down
-Outside paper comes off easily
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Spinforce Professional Table Tennis Racket - Competition Grade Ping Pong Paddle with Flared Handle - ITTF Tournament Approved Preassembled Table Tennis Rubber and Blade

text_fidelity_a:
Liberty Mountain Paracord BIG spool! I got the 3000 feet of "rainbow" paracord. Actually it's not rainbow because it's just alternating red, yellow, blue, and white. The colors look great though. Also, this isn't the regular 550 paracord we all know and love; this is thinner cord that has a coarser kermantle weave... It's comparable to something like 325 paracord or even 275 paracord, although I wish the kermantle was woven more finely like 550 cord. I suspect they did the coarser weave so the color pattern would be more pronounced. This paracord has only 2 inner strands. I do prefer finer woven 275 paracord from a different manufacturer but, hey, who can resist a 3000ft spool! One note, the description and the picture for 3000ft Rainbow listed the size of this paracord and 350lb "strength rating", however the listing was a bit confusing because other Rainbow options and other colors lacked descriptions or described normal 550 cord, and even showed showed images with packages that contradicted descriptions. Notwithstanding, overall I'm very pleased. There are specific uses where I prefer the thinner cord and this works great for that.

For size comparison, the second image shows this cord next to regular commercial 550 paracord.
text_fidelity_b: Liberty Mountain Paracord

What I did was just use the track nuts and the axle, I had to re-use the bearing races because they were designed specifically for the Deore hub. I flushed out the old lube and used Moly red lithium with a Timken OK load index of 55. I also installed new BC Precision bearings. text_fidelity_a:
Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer 2016 UPDATE: Every replacement tire for this trailer (12.5 inch tire) is total junk, except one: the [[ASIN:B00I3U8MSG Schwalbe HS158 Wheelchair Tire - Wire Bead (Grey - 12 1/2 x 2 1/4)]]. Trust me, I tried them all by now.
UPDATE:
After three years I decided to change the tires on this trailer. By luck I discovered that there exist 12.5 in scooter tires and pocket bike tires in widths of 2.5 and 2.75 inches. I opted for a pair of 2.75 knobby pocket bike tires in the hope that the added width would prevent some of tip overs I describe below. HUGE DIFFERENCE! I could still make this trailer tip with little difficulty but it is far more stable with the improved tires. So if you're considering this trailer be prepared to change the stock tires immediately (<$20x2 with free shipping if you shop carefully). You'll still want to run with low tire pressure but not nearly as low as with the stock tires. If you opt not to change the tires, read on so you know what to expect and read the comments, too.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
For what it is (the materials) this trailer seems over-priced. It sometimes tips over (often enough) traversing street and sidewalk surfaces via a handicap ramp and driveways (and vice versa). If and when it tips over the trailer doesn't take the bike (and you) with it, but if you are traversing from sidewalk to street, it tips in the middle of the intersection. Not good.

The trailer tires call for 35 PSI Max and if those tires are fully inflated with an empty load, this trailer will bounce all over creation at any larger imperfections in the riding surface and is at serious risk of tipping over.

The tilted, upward-leaning design approach (like a hand truck) is a good one because the footprint is small, it is easy to maneuver when un-hitched and one need not bend far over to access the trailer and its contents. The footprint is small enough so I sometimes take it on a transit bus without concern. But I believe the upward design, hitching to the seat post rather than the rear-wheel axle, as with most trailers, is the source of the stability problems.

The strapping system (2 are included) is just okay. You can do just as well or better with quality bungies. I bought some of the bags that Burley dedicates to this trailer but returned them. I now just cinch a plastic clothes hamper to the trailer with bungies and the hamper holds a ton.

A few things can be done to minimize the bouncing and tipping:

1. when unloaded, reduce the trailer tire pressure to 10 PSI or lower. The problem with this is if you go from empty to a moderate or full load in the same trip, you'll need to inflate the tires mid-trip, closer to max PSI to accommodate the additional load.

2. traverse driveways and handicap ramps completely perpendicular so that you don't catch a trailer tire on the ramp's raised shoulders.

3. slow down (a lot) in anticipation of any significant road imperfection for when 1 and 2 are difficult or impossible.

After close to two years I still use this trailer almost daily for shopping but I've learned to slow way down when traversing from sidewalk to street and keep my tire pressure to 10PSI or less when unloaded or with a light-to-moderate load to prevent tipping. Even with the PSI under 10, there are particular handicap ramps that I traverse frequently over which, if I don't slow down significantly, the trailer will tip over. Every time. No exaggeration.

I'm not completely sorry I own this trailer; it has a lot going for it: small footprint, carry-on size for air travel, etc, but I believe it needs some type of suspension to prevent tipping to make it a better value at $299.
text_fidelity_b: Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

text_fidelity_a: Nalgene Tritan Wide Mouth BPA-Free Water Bottle I've used all manner of bottles and containers for my outdoor activities, and they all were decent - unremarkable.  I had a low standard for plastic water bottles, and was content if I got three uses out of them before they fell apart or started leaking.  Ever since my first Nalgene bottle, I haven't looked back.  Special-purposes aside, the Nalegene Tritan Wide Mouth bottles have become THE STANDARD bottle for all of my use.  They of a significantly higher quality than previous bottles and canteens I've owned, and I appreciate the absence of Bisphenol-A.  They've survived ten times the abuse of bottles I've paid twice as much for.  The wide mouth has become essential, since I space became a premium for me while doing ultralite backpacking.  As well, the wide mouth makes it easier to use with my SteriPen and filters, and allows me to use it as a container when foraging for small edibles.  Partially filled with water, with an LED flashlight placed over it, the brighter-colored bottles make nice lanterns or signals at the campsite.  There's such a wide variety of colors available, to match most folks' styles - I'm partial to blues, gray, and black.  I'm quite pleased with their overall quality and versatility, and I only carry Nalgene bottles from now on.
text_fidelity_b: Nalgene Tritan Wide Mouth BPA-Free Water Bottle

text_fidelity_a:
Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black) NGL, it's a slick looking knife, but it isn't well constructed.

The blade looks good and the scales feel good in the hand. The blade definitely is sharp. The issue is the pivot point of the knife and the scales around the pivot point.

You'll notice that there is a nice index finger groove up near the pivot point. This is a nice ergo component, however when gripping the knife here the scales flex and cause a severe amount of blade play at the pivot point. Inversely, grabbing the blade towards the base and wigging it will cause the scales at that finger well to flex.

As much as I would like to write this off as a 1-off construction issue, I had an unrelated individual talk about the very same issue they had with this knife. They had sourced the knife from their local B&M and had mentioned the issue. I told them I had one in the mail and would check it when the knife showed up. Sure enough 2 instances of this knife with the same issue.

So buyer beware. I have heard good things about this knife maker and this knife so I decided to test the waters with this blade. I will be sending this knife back and I doubt I will be buying another Eafengrow even if it's another G-10 D2 for sub $20.
text_fidelity_b: Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black)

One in the 70s in Ohio that took out power for days to a large chunk of central Ohio.  Fortunately at that time the house had natural gas for the oven/stove so we could heat food/water and stand in front of the stove for warmth every few hours.  This past year in Texas, in an all electric house, I spent 5 days without power.  Because I had moved from Ohio to Texas, I had plenty of heavy blankets and warm winter clothing to keep me from freezing in a house that was near 20 degrees during the day and colder at night.  Since then, I have picked up items to ensure that I will NOT go through that again.  This little portable stove is one of those things.  I have a fire mat to put underneath it, but in case I'm without power, I can at least fire this up with some alcohol I bought for that purpose and heat some water for tea or warm up a can of soup.  I tried this out and it works great!  Not only can it make me a nice hot cup of tea, I can stand near it and get my hands warm.  Should I decide to go camping, I'll take this little stove as it is such a perfectly portable one!

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports TrailHead Sleeping Bag; Lightweight Camping, Hiking , Scout Green, 75" x 30" x 20" We ordered these bags for overnight/weekend backpacking trips. We aren't ultralight backpackers, since we stick to 1-2 nights, but this bag was still lighter than most we considered, so I was grateful for that. We have other Teton products that we use with car camping, so we are familiar with the company and their customer service and products.

First, the bags are fairly light at just 2lb 9 oz. Great for weekend backpackers. They also compress nicely in the sack they came with, but would do so even more if you bought a compression bag. However, they easily fit in the bottom sleeping bag compartment of our backpacks as is. The sack also has a strap on one end so you can easily attach it to the outside of your pack.

The bag is warm, and it's important to remember that sleeping bag ratings are for SURVIVAL and assume you're properly dressed for the weather you're using the bag in--dry base layer or naked, hat, etc. This bag should keep you comfortable at 40F and above if you're properly dressed/dry. If you go to bed in the same clothes you've been wearing all day, you'll get cold in any sleeping bag--always put on clean, dry clothes or sleep naked with a hat. :) If you're worried about warmth, you can easily add a lightweight fleece mummy bag liner--it won't add much weight to your pack, and the extra warmth can be reassuring if you need it.

I'm recovering from thyroid cancer and have gained 80lbs, so even as a plus size women at 5'10, 250 lbs, I have plenty of room to zip up and around me so that the bag isn't cold. I'm a side sleeper and I move around a lot at night, but I don't try to roll IN the bag--I roll with the bag. The cinch hood is a nice feature for a bag at this price.

Overall, yes, there are lighter and warmer backpacking bags--but for this price point, you'd be hard pressed to find one as warm, light, and soft as this one. If you're a beginner or just do 1-2 night trips from spring, summer, early fall, this bag should exceed your expectations. Add a lightweight fleece liner and you'll be set for even cooler temps. Teton never disappoints.
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports TrailHead Sleeping Bag; Lightweight Camping, Hiking , Scout Green, 75" x 30" x 20"

text_fidelity_a: G-Form Pro-S Compact Soccer Shin Guards - Football Shin Guards These shin guards are all one piece unlike the old traditional ones where the sleeve and guards are two separate pieces. text_fidelity_a:
Square36 NEW Exercise/Fitness Equipment Mat 12 Ft x 6 Ft. Highest Grade Materials. Our Fitness Mat Can Be Used For Cardio Workouts with or without shoes for fitness equipment We have been trying to up our game with exercise as Covid has gotten us out of the workout room and fully at home. When we added a heavy bag to make up for not being able to go back to our kickboxing guy we knew we needed something on the porch floor to protect our legs and feet. Based on existing reviews we knew we would be able to cut this if we needed to and that the thickness should be right. And with that hard cement we knew we wanted something to cushion us. So we chose this option.

It comes well wrapped in the included bag, strapped, and plastic. For our set up, the porch has a weird cut to it and we thought we’d have to cut the mat. Turns out we didn’t have to. The mat is thick enough to hold the heavy bag, but not so thick as to make it unsteady. We feel secure and we feel cushioned. Rolling it out we didn’t want the full amount, so we kept I partially rolled - so as to keep it away from the open end and any potential rain damage - and use the bag’s stand to hold the rest rolled in place. The width and length our perfect for this space and when we move we’ll have more or less depending - but not cutting it gives us options.

Working out on it has been fine. It gives security for footing - we do have one spot due to configuration, that makes it so we have to watch how far back we step, but it’s also not so high if we step funny we’ve had any issues. It gives good footing and we can punch full on - no worries. We are about to add a bench at the bottom end, that can be moved, so we’ll see how well that works, but based on the weight stand we’re confident it’ll be fine. We don’t know about marks it’ll leave - footprints from the weight of the stand or bench - but if we keep it in the same spot it’ll be fine.

Cleaning so far is easy - we have only had to wipe it down. We use our shoes on it and so far it’s been fine.

Overall we are really happy with this choice and think it’ll be a good mat for a long time, protecting us as we continue to workout.
text_fidelity_b: Square36 NEW Exercise/Fitness Equipment Mat 12 Ft x 6 Ft. Highest Grade Materials. Our Fitness Mat Can Be Used For Cardio Workouts with or without shoes for fitness equipment

text_fidelity_a: KiZHXlo Night Vision Binoculars for Darkness. Infrared Night Vision Goggles for Hunting and Surveillance.Take Day or Night IR Photos & Video from 400m/1300ft. Our row of houses has a wooded area behind them that belongs to the US Army Corps of Engineers which is a part of the lake that isn't too far from our houses.  We have coyotes, armadillos, raccoons and a few more critters that regularly visit our yards.  My neighbor was thrilled to try these out after I'd had the first try - I did see a coyote pass by my chain link fence at the back of my yard and I'm pretty sure the odd things I saw were armadillos...hard to tell exactly because they are faster than you'd think, but considering the humped back, I'm almost positive the three I saw were armadillos...this works well for what I wanted to use it for.  My lot is not terribly deep and the government sends out a bush hog about once a month to keep the woods from crowding too close to our back fences so there is a somewhat "clean" band or swath of about 10 to 12 feet they clear.  Keeps the critters from taking over, I'd imagine.  Anyway, my next door neighbor is positive that she has had armadillos trying to dig around the edge of her foundation - maybe looking for grubs?  I don't really know, but that's what she borrowed them for - to see if she could catch them in the act.  I explained how to use them and did tell her that they use a bunch of batteries so if they went off, it might be that the batteries would need recharging.  She said she had a bunch of AA's - the next day she told me she did not catch one scratching around her foundation, but that she did see a couple run by on her side yard.  I told her she could keep them for a few days to keep and eye out on her nocturnal "guests."  These night vision binoculars are rather cool, though this is my first time using any so I don't have anything to compare them with.  For me, I think the price point seems high, but again, this is my first pair.  I can say that they work for what I'm using them for - it is interesting to watch the night time creatures that live behind my house.
text_fidelity_b: KiZHXlo Night Vision Binoculars for Darkness. Infrared Night Vision Goggles for Hunting and Surveillance.Take Day or Night IR Photos & Video from 400m/1300ft.

text_fidelity_a:
Mountain House Chicken a la King with Noodles I am a VERY picky eater who doesn't like junk food, unhealthy food or Chef Boyardee anything that comes from a can. My father-in-law had a selection of Mountain House pouches and offered to let my husband and I try some as we were talking about camping food. He was already adding water to the Chicken a la King when I frowned at the selection. This is NOT the flavor I would have chosen to try but I kept my mouth shut. He handed me a small bowl of the food, which looked similar to the Lipton pasta pouches my husband ate when we were first married. I cautiously nibbled at a noodle. To my shock, it actually tasted good to me and I happily finished the whole bowl.

For reference, I'm a bit of a food snob. I cook most of my meals from scratch. I bake artisan breads and rolls for fun. I love Italian food and always make my own cream sauces from scratch. Sometimes I even make my own pasta. I maintain a small herb garden so I have access to organic, fresh-snipped herbs. Yeah, I'm that kind of food hobbyist. My picky tendencies thoroughly annoy my husband but he frequently gets to eat restaurant quality meals at home so he doesn't complain too much. Despite my picky palette, I STILL enjoyed the Chicken a la King! So much so that I bought a big #10 can for our hurricane kit.

If you like the flavor of a hearty, homemade chicken noodle soup with veggies, you are most likely going to like this meal. It has a light sauce instead of a soup broth but that description will give you a good idea about the flavor. My husband also liked the flavor very much but he's not nearly as picky as I am. Our 9 year old, who is somewhere in between our tastes and pickiness, also enjoyed the Chicken a la King and ate his portion eagerly. I'd say this is one meal that pleases just about everyone.

Tip: Use 1/4 cup less water than the pouches call for and let it sit for ten to fifteen minutes to soften the noodles properly. This goes for just about every Mountain House meal!
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Chicken a la King with Noodles

I got my wife a nice beach cruiser, my middle-school daughter a nice mountain bike with a rack so she can ride to school with her clarinet, my son a cheapie bike for a 6 year old to learn on, and myself a lower-end BMX to ride around the neighborhood with the family. Always had a love of the BMX style bike, and although I knew the one I got was a cheaper model, having Tony Hawk’s name on it was reassuring, and it had good reviews.

After 4 months of street/easy trail riding (that my 6 year old can do - not extreme or punishing on a bike), the right pedal arm fell off of the crank. It clamps down on a hex shaft, using a hex head bolt to tighten it, but as much as I could tighten the bolt it will not stay on. The crank assembly is also coming loose, and needs constant fighting in between reattachments of the right pedal.

This bike is going on the curb shortly, and I’ll be in the market for a higher quality BMX bike.

Could have been a fluke on this one. Maybe the tolerances from manufacturing were out of standard - whatever - but if you can toss in another hundred or two I would look for a higher quality bike.
text_fidelity_b: Dynacraft Childrens-Bicycles Tony Hawk

No mars on the one I received, received double boxed with lots of paper and angle cardboard to secure the wooden cabinet. This was excellent packing !
The boards on all sides, including the lid exactly 3/4" thick.
Powder storage: Fed. regulations state storage for over 20 pounds powder must be in wooden container that is not completely airtight sealed, boards must be 1" nominal thick. This box meets regulations, standard 1" nominal lumber boards is an actual 3/4" just like this box.
There are two lockable hasps, one on each side, which would take padlocks (not included). The hasps are fairly thin and so not burglar proof. Making it burglar proof might also make it sealed tight, which would not obey the standards to be open to the air. The boxes are required to be somewhat flimsy, I would say.
Can stack it 4 high with 1 pound powder containers, about 12 cans per layer = 48 pounds or so.

2 rope handles, one on each end.
For anyone desiring thicker sides, thin plywood sheets could be screwed down inside on each section of the box and lid, and secured with short 5/8" wood screws.
This same company makes smaller boxes, some of which are also available on Amazon.

I think this item is worth the money :)

text_fidelity_a:
Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Trunk Mounted Bike Rack, Black, One Size 3000 mile round trip with 2 road bikes at 85mph and we couldn't be happier. It took me about 3 minutes to figure out the install and another 3 minutes to load up the bikes. The rack holds extremely steady with virtually no movement from the bikes and requires little, if any, tightening once underway. Just as other user mentioned, we did have some damage to the lower bumper, a slight indention and a little peeling of the clear coat, but I don't hold that against this product. Really its just the ABS plastic bumper that was the issue and its hardly a problem. As for the trunk lid, there was absolutely no damage or markings at all. The color of the product is slightly misrepresented in the pictures - its more of a flat, colorless black composite than a shiny black color. Again, this is no issue for me, just not exactly what I expected. I will say, I'd guess this product could easily be painted to match your vehicle if you really wanted a cool, custom look. One other unexpected issue was the loss of MPG. We were driving a Honda Civic that regularly gets 30+mpg and that fell to 25-27mpg. Once more, no issue with the product, just something to be aware of for those on a longer drive.

On the whole, this rack is super easy to use, looks a LOT nicer than other racks, heavy enough to feel solid, light enough to store with ease. Over he course of our 3000 mile journey, I took this on and off 6 times and I never begrudged doing it. I would highly recommend this bike rack to anyone that asked.

Tips: Make sure the points of contact are clean before putting the rack on. This will ensure no dirt gets trapped and acts like sand paper once moving. Use small bungies or velcro straps to secure your front wheel from spinning and one more to secure the pedals of the two bikes to each other so the cranks don't turn. The security cable is a very nice touch that I would have no problem trusting for cross town and short stops, but I still added a standard, coated bike cable to secure it to the rack to feel more comfortable stopping overnight as the provided cable could very easily be cut with a small bolt cutter. Load your heavier bike on first to reduce the leverage placed on the rack. Take a short test run before going a long distance.
text_fidelity_b: Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Trunk Mounted Bike Rack, Black, One Size

text_fidelity_a:
Timbuk2 Espionage Camera Backpack, Black, Medium [[VIDEOID:13357c08e01ba23329875fbdce8b14b2]] Why I chose this bag:

-I wanted a backpack instead of an over-the-shoulder case because I find that a backpack is far more comfortable when walking long distances
-I was specifically looking for a case that had space for a laptop as well as non-camera related items. When I'm taking the bag with me on a plane I don't want to fully lose one of my carry-on bags to camera equipment. Further, given that this will be the bag I'm storing underneath the seat in front of me, it needs to have space to hold whatever I might want easy access to during the flight, such as a water bottle, food, books, iPad, magazines, jacket, phone charger, etc. Most of the backpack camera bags I looked at had suprsingly little room for non-camera equipment (except for a laptop).

The attached video gives a good idea of how much the bag can hold -- I've loaded it up and then unpacked it.

Pros:

-Tough, rugged construction. No doubt that it can take a beating and protect my camera.
-Even with a large body camera it should be able to hold three lenses (not including the lends attached to the camera).
-Holds laptop and has a good amount of space for non-camera equipment.
-Comes with rain cover; can hold tripod.

Cons:

-Most of the accessory pockets are ridiculously small. For example, the pocket meant for cell phones can barely fit an iPhone 5.

Overall I think this is an excellent bag, but the MSRP price is pretty steep. If it wasn't for the fact that I was able to get the bag for 40% off the MSRP thanks to a one day sale, I would have purchased one of Timbuk2's cheaper camera bags, such as the [[ASIN:B00AMXVKLI Sleuth]] or [[ASIN:B004VD7QU4 Snoop]]. Despite the high price, I'm still going to give the Espionage five starts because it is such a well made camera bag.
text_fidelity_b: Timbuk2 Espionage Camera Backpack, Black, Medium

RAVE Sports Northern Lites Backcountry Snowshoe Speed Binding, Black, One Size Only the 2nd pair of snowshoes owned over the past +30 years. The old Sherpas are fine, but have been lusting over a pair of NorthernLites Backcountry for years. YOLO. Splurge. Outside of a significant weight savings, the binding system is nicer than the old Sherpas. Simple to put on or remove even with gloved hands. Only fiddling was tucking away the speed binding lace. Couple loops around the heel strap before tightening it.

Just in from the 4th hike. Logging an average of +9km per hike over rolling terrain in 6-12" of fresh light powder like snow. At 60kg these shoes are a bit on the too large size. Personal preference for 30"ers. The shoes track nice. Traction going up and down hill is good. Traversing a steeper face is a bit of an issue. No heel lift platform becomes an issue on longer, steeper climbs. Hit a short section of trail that was groomed for fat tire bikes. Real hard packed groomed. Shoe from some people trail runners left a minimal imprint. Left the snowshoes on for the couple hundred meters. Traction was excellent.

Expectations are for a durable product based on the past history of this brand of snowshoe.

Good for those looking for a light weight, easy on/off snowshoe for use in rolling terrain in fresh snow.
text_fidelity_b: RAVE Sports Northern Lites Backcountry Snowshoe Speed Binding, Black, One Size

Grizzly Gear Emergency Survival Mylar Thermal 2 Person Sleeping Bag - Accommodates 2 Adults - 64" X 87" As you know, the point of these emergency blankets is to use them when everything else has failed. You are not at home (or the power and gas is out), you can't get to relatives, a hotel, or a Red Cross shelter... Or perhaps you are literally lost in the woods and thanking your lucky stars you threw an emergency blanket in your daypack..

The only difference here is that two people can fit, and if you have ever had to worry about hyperthermia, you know that the body heat of another is about the only way to bring up the body heat of the severely chilled person.

On a trail crew as an older teen and we got one guy into a fairly serious hyperthermia situation after using a cold mountain lake to float materials for trail bridges a shorter distance than hiking them around the lake. Great idea, but several us of took too many trips. We had a sleeping bag with us in a day kit, but it lost most of its thermal capacity when it got wet from the guys soaked clothes (dumb us: take the wet clothes off first!...) One of these emergency blankets and with room for a second person would have been an easier way to get him back to normal, and taken a lot less space.

From a price point of view, you can find single blankets for $5 to $20 bucks, depending on sale prices, quality and so forth. Thus, this double-sized version is priced at essentially no difference in cost and works for two. Construction is great. Four stars only because it's not a super premium version (which of course would cost more.) (EDITED to five stars, responding to a comment -- I agree.) These are designed for emergencies, so you are not buying this for multiple uses. This version seems to be at the right price point.

Hope this is helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Grizzly Gear Emergency Survival Mylar Thermal 2 Person Sleeping Bag - Accommodates 2 Adults - 64" X 87"

text_fidelity_a:
Kowela ab Trainer Ab Roller Wheel for Abdominal Muscle Training, Abdominal Exercise Equipment, Perfect Abdominal core Carver Fitness Workout for Abdominal Muscles There are many positive Amazon reviews on this ab roller. And there are definitely some good points for sure.

The wheel is WIDE. So it's very stable during movements. The width also allows easy turns. So you can create a variety of angles for your ab workouts. It also has a spring mechanism that prevents the roller from over-extending. Therefore keeps you from hyper-extending! Or at least that's the concept.

However, my main concern, is with the construction.

It's made entirely of plastic (namely the handles) with a thin tread of rubber to act as the gripping portion of the wheel. Although there is a "metal" rod that acts as the axle, I'm not sure if it's steel. And during use, you are exerting A LOT of force on these plastic handles. And while it appears that they are sturdy, something feels just a little questionable. The rolling mechanism is not smooth. As if the handles may give out mid-exercise.

I would have preferred steel & rubber for the axle/handle assembly. It would have just felt more durable/comfortable. And I'm not sure if there are any bearings, but this would have at least taken the friction off of the axle. As it appears to be rolling directly against the plastic of the wheel. Of course, this unit is under $30.00. So possibly that's not to be expected at this price point.

However, you don't want your mind focused on the quality of your exercise equipment while your working out. So if that's at all a concern for you, possible consider a higher end ab roller (if such a thing exists!).
text_fidelity_b: Kowela ab Trainer Ab Roller Wheel for Abdominal Muscle Training, Abdominal Exercise Equipment, Perfect Abdominal core Carver Fitness Workout for Abdominal Muscles

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) This is a great concept. I never purchased the original fitbit because I wanted a heart rate feature. The problem is the heart rate accuracy during CrossFit/HIIT/strenuous-type exercises. The accuracy is spot on during the day, and seems equally accurate during mundane exercises (running, cycling, rowing machine, etc). The inaccuracies show up during virtually any other style of workout. I have corresponded a substantial amount with fitbit, and they say they are working on improving the algorithms. Who knows if they can figure it out.

While I would like to see it being accurate during my workouts, one of my biggest complaints regarding it's accuracy is the "lag time". Meaning, how long after the activity is over does the fitbit take to begin showing an accurate heart rate. I would think a few seconds is reasonable. Well, it takes 30-45 minutes!! I don't understand why, and fitbit was unable/unwilling to tell me why. I have tried wearing it on both wrists, at varying tightnesses and locations on my wrists, and taking it off for a few minutes and then putting it back on. Nothing helps, it still takes 30+ minutes for it to be accurate again.

So how is it inaccurate? It reads REALLY low. It will typically read 50-60 bpm low during and immediately after an intense workout. My actual heart rate is 160-180 and the fitbit will say 95-110.

I gave it 3 stars because everything else about it is great and useful. So if your workouts are walking/running/cycling or other similar types of activites, it will work great for you. For those doing similar exercises as me, it will only be useful for monitoring heart rate throughout the day and while sleeping. I decided that was useful enough to keep it, though it was close. It becomes a personal decision as to the value of it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Manduka PRO Pro:
- warrantee
- durability
- thickness
- comfort
- length options
- no weird smell

Cons
- Price
- weight
- slickness

So, the mat MUST be salted and let sit once you first get it, otherwise it will be very slick. Do not skimp in the salt.

The price for the mat is high, but it has a lifetime warrantee and last FAR longer than most other mats.

It is not as soft as some other mats I have used, but it also isn't squishy like a lot of cheaper mats. I have great stability on the mat (once it has been salted). It is cushioned enough that I can do table and the like on my knees without too much discomfort (yay, old knees).

It is heavy. This is not a mat I would want to use for a long walk to the studio. It is great for home or if you always have close parking.

As a taller person, I really liked that this mat is very long. It adds to the weight, but it means I don't have to adjust where I am on the mat most of the time.

Unlike some mats, this one does not have the weird smell, or at least I did not notice one after salting.
text_fidelity_b: Manduka PRO

I don't have any hesitation cooking on it, would love to eat some bacon cooked on this over wood fire, but the question is it worth the price? I think it could be depending on what you want it for.
